gaps.note: the interior under the top cover is drawn from one top-down photograph. Drawn: the cover (it lifts off), the board, eight DIMMs, a heatsink, the air shroud and the supply cage cover (both lift off), six fans, one of the two stacked internal drives, and standing in from the front bays the two supplies, both risers and any cards in their slots. Not drawn: the power distribution board between the drive cage and the supplies (a plain panel here), the optional second shroud for a GPU card, and cabling. THE AIR SHROUD IS ESTIMATED from an isometric figure, and its mouth at the fans is cut short. The heatsink is the SYS-111E-WR part placed on the socket; this server is photographed with the socket empty. The two risers are the WR's outlines turned to face the front; this server's own bracket arm is narrower on its photograph.

chassis.note: Product page, datasheet and manual agree: 1.7 x 17.2 x 16.9 in, 43 x 437 x 429 mm, 1U, chassis CSE-515B-R601W. 437 is the body between the ear folds on the front image. No document says what the depth runs between.

compliance.note: Product page: "NEBS Level 3 Certified" as a key feature. Manual section 2.8: the SYS-111E-FDWTR is DC-I and can be grounded in both CBN and IBN networks.

ears.note: THE EARS ARE NOT DRAWN. On the front image each ear with its handle runs about 70 px outside the body, 21 mm. Everything on this face is on the body.

environmental.note: Product page and manual Appendix C: operating 0 to 40 C, non-operating -40 to 70 C on the product page and -40 to 60 C in the manual; operating relative humidity 8 to 90% non-condensing, non-operating 5 to 95%. THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE on the upper non-operating temperature; the manual's lower figure is carried and the disagreement is a gap.

faces.note: Bottom, left and right are sized from the stated dimensions and declared empty: no document held shows any of them straight on.

front.note: Left to right: the two DC supplies, PWS2 at 5.6 and PWS1 at 62.8; from 118.3 the I/O plate - a vent field around the power button (centre 141.3, 12.6), the serial port, the BMC LAN port over two USB 2.0 ports, a second vent field over two USB 3.2 ports, LAN1 and LAN2 (10GbE), VGA and a small vent block, with a row of slots along the bottom edge under all of it; above LAN2 and VGA the slot 3 window; from 298 the slot 1 and 2 bracket; and the end bracket from 418 with a round hole. Names and order are the manual's figure 1-1 and System Features: Front table.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT IMAGE FAILS THE PANEL GATE AND IS READ AS FRACTIONS ON EACH AXIS. It is a photograph from slightly above: 1465 px across for 437 mm (3.352 px/mm) and 134.5 px down for 43 mm (3.128), 7% apart. Across positions are read at 3.352 px/mm; down positions are fractions of the 43 mm height. The check on it is another server: the SYS-111E-WR carries the sibling board (X13SEW-F) behind an I/O plate measured off a different photograph, and the two agree on where everything on that plate is to 1.5 mm - serial port 149.4 here against 148.2 there, BMC port 174.5 / 173.6, USB 2.0 175.1 / 173.7, USB 3.2 192.6 / 192.2, LAN1 211.5 / 210.1, LAN2 230.2 / 228.8, VGA 257.6 / 256.2, slot 3 window 230.2..293.6 / 230.6..292.5, thumbscrew 310.3 / 309.2. THE I/O PLATE IS DRAWN AT THE WR FIGURES, which come from the better-scaled image; what is this server's own is read off its own image.

gate-1-rear.note: The rear image is straight on and nearly passes: 1928 px across for 437 mm (4.412 px/mm) and 179 px down for 43 mm (4.163), 5.6% apart, which is more than the gate allows, so it too is read per axis. The vent columns give an even pitch right across it, 27.3 px, 6.19 mm.

ground-stud.note: The manual's section 2.8 says both the AC and DC servers carry a chassis ground terminal marked with the protective earth symbol, and its figure 2-8 circles a stud in the front vent field, above the gap between the USB 3.2 ports and LAN1. THE FIGURE IS A CROPPED LINE DRAWING WITH NO SCALE OF ITS OWN: taking its USB port as 13.1 mm wide puts the stud 11.4 right of the USB 3.2 centre and 11.8 above the upper port, at (203.6, 11.7). The front photograph does not show a stud there - that field is plain vents on it - so the position rests on the drawing alone. The heading says studs; the figure shows one.

interior.note: THE TOP VIEW IS THE CHASSIS UNDER ITS TOP COVER, rear at the top; the cover (supermicro/system-cover-sc515b@1) is seated and comes off in the viewer. The interior is read off the top-down photograph of the open SYS-111E-FDWTR embedded in its manual MNL-2570 on page 13 (1419 x 1381 at 300 ppi), on which the chassis is 1254 px across for 437 mm (2.870 px/mm) and 1236 px front to rear for 429 (2.881), 0.4% apart, so it passes the panel gate. Positions are read at 2.875 px/mm from the left wall and the rear wall. The board lies 120.6..323.6 across and 86.8..416.8 front to rear, turned I/O-forward; the six fans stand in a row 14 from the rear, four together from 149.0 on a 43.1 pitch and two more at 335.4 and 378.5 - DRAWN ON ONE PITCH WITH ONE BREAK: the six read 149.0, 192.1, 235.3, 278.4, 335.4 and 379.9 on the photograph, and the last is drawn 1.4 nearer its neighbour to keep the pitch, which is inside what a fan housing edge reads to. THE GAP BETWEEN THE FOURTH AND FIFTH IS REAL, 17 mm of chassis with a mounting post each side of it on the photograph, where the others stand 3 mm apart; the two-drive cage is at the rear left, 2.9..110 across; the supplies run 220 back from the front wall. Parts that stand up off the floor are nearer the camera and read a few millimetres outward of where they are, so the supplies are placed from the front view's bays, not from this image. THE SUPPLIES, THE RISERS AND THE CARDS PROJECT INTO THIS VIEW from their front bays through each bay's `plan:`, turned half a turn (`rotate: 180`) because a plan is drawn face-at-the-top and these face the front.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-04 for an end-of-life notice (Supermicro's product page, which still offers the system, and the web for "SYS-111E-FDWTR end of life"); none found.

power.note: NO SYSTEM POWER FIGURE IS STATED on the product page, the datasheet, the manual or the quick reference guide; each gives the supply rating only, and no Lot 9 addendum is published for this model. A supply rating is not the server's draw.

power-button.note: The manual calls it the Power Button with Status LED: the main power switch, with a lamp that is lit when the system is operating normally and flashes on drive activity. It is supermicro/power-button-sc515b@1, centred where the image puts it.

psus.note: Product page and manual Appendix B: two PWS-601S-1R, 600 W, -44 to -65 Vdc, redundant; front table: PWS1 on the right, PWS2 on the left. Both are seated by default.

rear.note: A field of square vents, 4.8 on a 6.19 pitch across and 6.2 down, starting 7.1 from the left and 4.05 from the top: six rows over the first 46 columns, where the six fans stand behind it, and the lower three rows only over the next 22, under a plain plate. The manual's rear figure labels the fans and a service tag. THE SERVICE TAG IS NOT DRAWN: only its edge shows, under the bottom of the face at about 365..395; see the gap.

slots.note: Product page: 1 PCIe 5.0 x16 LP slot and 2 PCIe 5.0 x16 FHFL slots; manual Expansion Slot Locations table: 1 and 2 full-height full-length, 3 low-profile. The slots are bays of the two riser parts this server shares with the SYS-111E-WR (see those parts for the check). ONE DIFFERENCE IS NOT CARRIED: slot 3 here is a full x16, where the WR's is x8 in an x16 connector, and the shared riser part states x8 lanes. See the gap.

sources.note: Read for this model: Supermicro's product page for the SYS-111E-FDWTR (supermicro.com/en/products/system/iot/1u/sys-111e-fdwtr) and its two-page datasheet, for dimensions, weight, ports, slots, power supply, environmentals and the NEBS statement; the User's Manual MNL-2570 revision 1.0d, which covers this server and its two AC siblings (SYS-111E-FWTR, SYS-111E-FWTR-EU), for the front and rear views, feature tables, the grounding section and Appendix B; the quick reference guide QRG-2570; the SC515B chassis manual; and the X13SEW motherboard manual MNL-2413. The two images measured are both embedded in the manual at 300 ppi: the front on page 10 (1767 x 444) and the rear on page 12 (1946 x 205). No vendor 3D model is on the product page, NetBox's devicetype-library has no entry, and a web search for a square-on photograph of the front found none.

weight.note: Product page: net weight 10.01 lbs (4.54 kg), gross 14.99 lbs (6.8 kg), for the barebone.
